newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine taken into hospital - BBC.
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine taken into hospital - BBC.

text.p: Former British deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine was on Saturday taken into hospital for observation and tests, the BBC reported.

Heseltine, a frontrunner to lead the opposition Conservative Party following the resignation of John Major as party leader, lost his government post after the Labour Party under Tony Blair swept to a landslide victory in the May 1 election.
Heseltine, 64, was taken into the Horton General Hospital in Banbury, central England, for observation over the weekend. His condition was described as comfortable, the BBC said.
Four years ago, Heseltine suffered a heart attack while on holiday in Venice, but he made a full recovery.
Heseltine has been named as favourite to succeed Major as leader of the Conservative Party following its crushing defeat at the hands of Labour.
Conservative Party Central Office said it was checking the report.
